title: Shadow Traffic: Policy Engine / RoutePolicy integration working notes
content:
Context / goal
- We need RoutePolicy + Policy Engine representation for “Shadow Traffic” so we can mirror a sampled subset of live requests to 1+ shadow targets WITHOUT impacting primary responses.
- The policy must be:
  - deterministic at request time (same inputs -> same decision)
  - safe-by-default (shadow off unless explicitly enabled)
  - enforceable at the edge/data-plane (cannot rely only on Console)
  - bounded (budget/rate limit/capacity caps; cardinality-safe tags)

Non-goals (for policy layer)
- Policy engine does NOT implement judging/scoring logic; it only selects where shadow goes + what metadata to attach.
- Policy engine does NOT store payloads; only emits config that downstream components may use for redaction/retention.


Key requirements from stakeholders
- PM (Paula/Marissa): must support per-route shadowing config w/ allowlists (customer/org), region constraints, sampling %, and targeting model/version/quant profile/prompt config.
- SRE (Sean): must have kill switch + hard caps; shadow failures must never affect primary latency/SLO.
- Security (Naomi): must respect data residency + retention defaults; allow customers to opt out and/or disable logging.


Where does the decision happen?
Current thinking: decision happens in Policy Engine evaluation for a route, returning both:
1) primary target decision (existing)
2) shadow execution decision (new): list of shadow targets + sampling decision + guardrails metadata

We need the sampling decision to happen once and be attached to the request (request_id) so we can join primary/shadow later and avoid double-sampling in retries.

Open question: edge vs runtime
- If sampling is at gateway: easiest to ensure “doesn’t touch runtime batching/KV cache”, but adds fan-out complexity and requires request copy.
- If sampling is at runtime: less duplication of request parsing, but needs strict isolation + queue/backpressure.
- ADR direction (latest): runtime triggers enqueue to shadow runner; policy engine just decides “shadow_enabled + params” and data-plane is responsible for async.


Policy schema proposal (RoutePolicy additions)
Notes: naming bikeshed. We want this to be consistent with other RoutePolicy sub-blocks (e.g., routing, auth, rate limits).

Proposed top-level block (per route): shadow_traffic
- shadow_traffic.enabled: bool (default false)
- shadow_traffic.mode: "async" only for MVP (explicitly disallow sync)
- shadow_traffic.sample_rate: float [0.0..1.0] (default 0.0)
- shadow_traffic.max_qps: integer (optional) OR integrate w/ existing quotas system (preferred)
- shadow_traffic.customer_allowlist: list<string> (customer_id or org_id) (optional)
- shadow_traffic.customer_blocklist: list<string> (optional)
- shadow_traffic.region_allowlist: list<string> (optional) (e.g. "us-east", "eu-west")
- shadow_traffic.shadow_targets: list<ShadowTarget> (1..N)
- shadow_traffic.redaction_profile: string enum ("default" / "strict" / "none"??) (security wants “no raw by default”)
- shadow_traffic.retention_tier: string enum ("none" / "7d" / "30d" / "custom") (may live outside policy, but needs to be referenced)
- shadow_traffic.debug_logging: bool (default false; only allowed for internal + explicitly approved accounts)

ShadowTarget object fields (conceptually; actual stored representation may be flattened)
- name: short identifier (required; used for metrics tag; must be from allowlist to control cardinality)
- model_ref: string (model + version pointer) OR “routing target id”
- quant_profile: string (optional)
- prompt_config_ref: string (optional; e.g., system prompt variant)
- traffic_weight: float (optional; within shadow-only; default equal split)
- judge_profile: string (optional; config id consumed by eval harness)
- timeout_ms: int (shadow-only timeout; MUST NOT affect primary)

Cardinality guardrail note
- “name” must be short and from an allowlist. Do NOT allow arbitrary “experiment_id” strings from customers to end up in metric labels.
- For customer-provided experiment ids, we should store as dimension only in logs/events w/ strict sampling and/or hashing, not as metric tag.


Default behavior / safe defaults
- If shadow_traffic.enabled is unset -> treated as false
- If enabled=true but sample_rate missing -> treated as 0.0 (force explicit)
- If sample_rate > 0 but no shadow_targets -> validation error (policy rejected at publish time)
- If shadow_targets present but enabled=false -> ignored (no shadow)
- If route is in “private / regulated” mode and customer has opted out of shadowing -> forced disable regardless of route config
- If global kill switch is ON -> forced disable
- If per-customer kill switch is ON -> forced disable
- If budget exhausted (rate limit / queue backpressure) -> shadow is dropped; primary unaffected; emit drop metric


Allowlist / blocklist semantics (customer targeting)
We need deterministic semantics when both allowlist + blocklist are present.
Proposed:
- Evaluate “eligible_customer” as:
  - if blocklist contains customer_id -> NOT eligible
  - else if allowlist is empty -> eligible (subject to other constraints)
  - else if allowlist contains customer_id -> eligible
  - else -> NOT eligible

Notes:
- For enterprise, they want “opt-in allowlist” by default during beta. We can implement by setting allowlist explicitly.
- Customer_id source of truth: we should use internal account/org id attached to auth context (not user-provided headers).


Region semantics
- Region allowlist should be evaluated against the serving region of the primary request.
- For data residency: the shadow target execution must remain within allowed residency boundaries.
  - If the primary request is served in EU region and policy tries to shadow to a US-only shadow target -> must be rejected at policy publish time if detectable, or forced drop at runtime.

Open question:
- Do we allow shadow targets in different region for “cross-region quality comparison”? Security likely says no for any payload-containing processing. Maybe allow for “prompt/metadata-only” modes later, but MVP: keep same region.


Sampling decision details
We need a stable coin flip per request.
Proposed: sample = hash64(request_id + shadow_sampling_salt + route_id) / 2^64 < sample_rate
- request_id: generated on gateway, propagated end-to-end
- shadow_sampling_salt: per-environment secret to prevent predictability; rotated occasionally
- route_id: included so that the same request hitting different routes doesn’t correlate

Retries
- If request retried with same request_id, sampling result is stable.
- If request_id changes on retry, sampling may change (acceptable).

Multiple shadow targets
- If sample is true, we may run all targets (N) or choose subset based on per-target weights.
- For MVP: run all configured targets but cap N (e.g., max 2 or 3) to contain cost.
  - Later: weighted selection and “only one shadow target per request” option.

Validation rules (publish-time)
- sample_rate must be within [0..1]
- enabled implies sample_rate > 0 AND at least 1 target
- max shadow targets per route: propose 3 (hard)
- target.name must match regex ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$
- target.name uniqueness within a route
- model_ref must be resolvable (exists in model catalog) OR allow “pending” during draft but block publish


Budgets + quotas integration
We have two approaches:
A) Add shadow_traffic.max_qps/max_concurrency to RoutePolicy and enforce in shadow runner.
B) Use existing quotas/budget primitives (preferred; consistent with other features).

Preferred direction:
- Policy engine emits a “shadow_budget_key” derived from (customer_tier, region, route_id) and maybe “shadow_feature”.
- Shadow runner consults budget service / rate limiter with that key.
- Need to ensure we do not create per-customer-per-route high-cardinality keys in the budget service if it can’t handle it.

Compromise:
- Budget key scoped to (customer_id, region) for enterprise only; otherwise scope to (tier, region) or (project_id, region).
- Add admin-level caps: global shadow qps cap per region.

SRE note
- We need a “drop shadow immediately” behavior when queue depth high.
- Policy engine should not attempt dynamic decisions based on queue depth (avoid dependency). Shadow runner should do that.


Kill switch layers
We need at least:
1) global kill switch (env-wide)
2) per-route disable (route config)
3) per-customer disable (support/security)
4) per-region cap/disable (ops)

Implementation detail
- Global/per-region/per-customer likely stored in a fast config store (feature flag / admin control plane).
- Policy engine should incorporate them in evaluation so data-plane receives a simple “shadow_enabled=false” outcome.
- However, to avoid tight coupling, shadow runner should ALSO honor kill switch (defense-in-depth).


What does Policy Engine output to the data-plane?
Proposed “computed policy” fields returned with route decision:
- shadow.enabled (bool)
- shadow.sampled (bool) (this is the deterministic coin flip result)
- shadow.targets (list of resolved targets, bounded)
- shadow.policy_version (string / hash)
- shadow.redaction_profile (enum)
- shadow.retention_tier (enum)
- shadow.audit_tags (small set; e.g., customer_tier, route_name_bucket)

Important: do not attach full allowlists/blocklists to request context (sensitive + large).


Metrics / observability tags (policy responsibilities)
We need to keep a tight set of dimensions to avoid cardinality blow-ups.
Allowed tags for shadow_eval.* should be derived from:
- route_bucket (not raw route name if it’s customer-defined)
- primary_model_family (bucketed)
- shadow_target_name (bounded)
- region
- customer_tier (free/scale/enterprise)
- sampling_bucket (e.g., 0.1%, 1%, 5%, 10%)

Do NOT tag metrics with:
- raw customer_id
- request_id
- prompt hash
- experiment_id (unless heavily bucketed)

Open question
- route_bucket definition: do we maintain a mapping table in control plane (route_id -> stable bucket label)? If so, ensure it’s stable and not editable by customers.


Security / privacy knobs in policy
We need to be explicit about what policy can and cannot express.
Proposed:
- “redaction_profile” is a reference to a server-defined config, not an arbitrary JSON from customers.
- Profiles define what payload fields can be logged/stored for shadow runs:
  - default: store derived metrics only; do not store full prompt/output
  - strict: store minimal metadata only (no content); maybe disable judge that needs content
  - approved_debug: allow limited sampled payload capture, requires internal approval (INT ticket)

Note: Applied ML wants access to content for judge scoring. We should assume judge happens in-memory and only the judge result is stored by default. Any content persistence requires explicit policy + customer consent.


Interaction with Smart Routing
Potential conflict: smart routing might change primary model; shadow wants to compare to candidate(s).
We should define:
- primary selection happens normally.
- shadow targets are evaluated AFTER primary selection.
- shadow targets may be specified as:
  - absolute model_ref (explicit)
  - relative variant (e.g., “same family as primary but quant=fp8”) (future)

MVP: absolute model_ref only.


Example (rough) RoutePolicy snippet (for discussion only)
route: /v1/chat/completions
shadow_traffic:
  enabled: true
  sample_rate: 0.01
  customer_allowlist: ["org_8f3...", "org_2aa..."]
  region_allowlist: ["us-east", "us-west"]
  redaction_profile: "default"
  retention_tier: "7d"
  shadow_targets:
    - name: "llama3_70b_fp8_candidate"
      model_ref: "llama-3-70b-instruct@2025-10-01"
      quant_profile: "fp8"
      judge_profile: "shadow-judge-v1"

Validation: name ok; target count 1; sample_rate 1%


Open questions / TODOs
- Do we need “shadow only on specific request types” (streaming vs non-streaming; tool-calling) in policy? Might be important to avoid judge failures.
- How to handle requests with customer-provided tool schemas (highly variable) and metric cardinality? Probably fine if metrics don’t tag tool name.
- If judge_profile is set but redaction_profile=strict (no content), do we disable judge automatically or reject config?
- Confirm whether customer_allowlist should be org_id or project_id (product leaning org_id; platform prefers account_id).
- What’s the migration strategy for existing routes? Default off, no behavior change.


Action items (as of last sync)
- Ethan: write up validation rules + propose max targets + name constraints; sync w/ Thomas (cardinality) (ETA 11/01)
- Benji: draft protobuf/schema changes for RoutePolicy.shadow_traffic (ENG-2420) (ETA 11/05)
- Jordan: confirm deterministic sampling hash inputs + where request_id generated/propagated (ties to eng-platform thread 1731426800)
- Cole: propose budget keying strategy that won’t melt quotas service (review with SRE) (ENG-2440 dependency)
- Naomi: confirm redaction_profile defaults + what’s allowed for beta accounts


Meeting notes (highlights)
2025-10-22 (policy + SRE)
- SRE asks: “shadow must be droppable at any point; never waits on queue.”
- Decision: policy returns sampled=true/false but runtime can override (drop) if budget/queue says no.

2025-11-07 (policy + security)
- Security: default retention should be metrics-only; content capture requires explicit opt-in and restricted access.
- Add requirement: policy publish-time check blocks debug_logging unless customer is in approved list.

2025-11-18 (policy + product)
- Product wants customers to reason about “Shadow Targets” in Console; asks that target.name be customer-visible.
- Pushback: if customer can set arbitrary names, cardinality risk. Proposed compromise: customer-visible label stored in Console metadata; metrics tag uses bounded internal name.
